hints: Find the velocity expression by differentiating displacement $s(t)$ with respect to time $t$.
Use the power rule $\frac{d}{dt}(t^n) = n t^{n-1}$ to get $v = \frac{5}{2}t^{1/2} - \frac{45}{8}t^{-1/2}$.
Set $v = 0$ to find when the particle is at rest, multiplying by $t^{1/2}$ to solve $\frac{5}{2}t = \frac{45}{8}$.
Substitute the non-zero time $t = \frac{9}{4}$ back into the displacement function $s(t)$ to find $s$.
walkthrough:
State the calculus relationship between velocity and displacement: velocity is the time derivative of displacement:
$$v = \frac{ds}{dt}$$

Apply the power rule of differentiation $\frac{d}{dt}(t^n) = n t^{n-1}$ to each term:
$$\frac{d}{dt}(t^{5/2}) = \frac{5}{2}t^{5/2 - 1} = \frac{5}{2}t^{1/2}$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\left(-\frac{15}{4}t^{3/2}\right) = -\frac{15}{4} \times \frac{3}{2}t^{3/2 - 1} = -\frac{45}{8}t^{-1/2}$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}(6) = 0$$
$$v = \frac{5}{2}t^{1/2} - \frac{45}{8}t^{-1/2}$$

Set velocity equal to zero to find the instant the particle comes to rest:
$$\frac{5}{2}t^{1/2} - \frac{45}{8}t^{-1/2} = 0$$

Multiply the entire equation by $t^{1/2}$ (valid since $t > 0$):
$$\frac{5}{2}t - \frac{45}{8} = 0$$
$$\frac{5}{2}t = \frac{45}{8}$$

Multiply both sides by $\frac{2}{5}$ to isolate $t$:
$$t = \frac{45}{8} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{90}{40} = \frac{9}{4} = 2.25\text{ s}$$

Substitute $t = \frac{9}{4}$ back into the original displacement formula:
$$s = \left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{5/2} - \frac{15}{4}\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{3/2} + 6$$

Evaluate each power carefully using $\sqrt{9/4} = 3/2$:
$$\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{3/2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$$
$$\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{5/2} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^5 = \frac{243}{32}$$
$$-\frac{15}{4} \times \frac{27}{8} = -\frac{405}{32}$$
$$6 = \frac{192}{32}$$
$$s = \frac{243 - 405 + 192}{32} = \frac{30}{32} = \frac{15}{16}\text{ m}\quad (0.9375\text{ m})$$
